summary: Streaming stalls and request timeouts for requests with very large input + high max_tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FathomAI Labs reports streaming responses hang and eventually timeout when sending requests that combine a very large prompt (40k-90k tokens) with high max_tokens (50k+). The requests either stop producing tokens mid-stream and client sees a socket/read timeout, or the API returns a 504 after ~120s. Customer reports this started after last week's runtime kernel update (deploy r3456).

Impact:
- Affected production traffic for the customer on rw-instruct-70b-v1 and rw-instruct-13b-quant.
- Several customer sessions stalled; feature in their product that relies on streaming completions became unusable.
- Business impact: regression blocked a rollout; customer has paused live experiments.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1 region
- Customer using hosted Redwood API with token-based auth and streaming SSE endpoint (/v1/stream).
- Observed on both dedicated and hosted shared pools for this customer.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) POST to /v1/stream with prompt containing ~60k tokens (concatenated logs + context)
2) Set max_tokens=60000 and temperature=0.2
3) Expect streaming chunks within 1-3s; instead client receives initial tokens then streaming stalls after ~18-30s and eventually socket times out, or API returns 504.

Observed logs and telemetry snippets:
- Customer trace-id: trace-cust-7a2f
- Proxy logs show long-lived connections and intermittent chunked writes stop being produced. Example: "[stream_writer] connection 0x7f9a stalled at seq 128, last_chunk_ts=2026-03-09T21:14:03Z"
- Serving runtime logs (linked): datadog: https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=trace-cust-7a2f
- Kernel selector commit r3456 changed sequence-kernel heuristics (PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/987)

Notes to reproduce in staging (support):
- Reduced reproduction with smaller numbers: prompt 20k tokens + max_tokens 25k will reproduce stall consistently in isolated staging pool when using rw-instruct-13b-quant.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Cap max_tokens to <= 25k and split very large prompts into smaller windowed requests. This avoids the stall for now but affects latency and requires client-side engineering changes.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Aisha (Support): Logged ticket after customer provided traces. Customer says incident began after last kernel update. Assigned to infra SRE for triage.

2026-03-10 11:03 - Liam (SRE): I reproduced a stall in staging using rw-instruct-13b-quant with prompt 25k tokens + max_tokens=30k. Initial hypothesis: flushing/streaming buffer interaction with the new kernel path causes blocking when KV cache grows beyond ~30M entries.

2026-03-10 13:45 - Engineering (runtime team): We see elevated GC and websocket write timeouts in the same window. Attaching profiling run: github.com/redwood/serving/issue/9152/profile-run-20260310. Noting that kernel r3456 modifies async token emission ordering under large sequence lengths.

2026-03-10 15:10 - Liam (SRE): Rolled back kernel selector in a staging pool; reproduction no longer occurs under identical input. This points to regression in r3456. Preparing a bisect to find exact change.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Customer (FathomAI): Acknowledged workaround (capping tokens) but requests ETA for permanent fix as this blocks a new feature. Asking for SLA credit if resolution exceeds 72 hours.

2026-03-11 14:22 - Engineering: Bisect narrowed to change in commit 3456 -> file kernel/seq_optimizer.cpp around async_flush() changes. Hypothesis: when KV cache cross-threshold, async_flush waits for pending batch callbacks that are lost in some scheduling interleavings, leaving stream_writer pending indefinitely.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Product/Support: Notified customer of root cause hypothesis and proposed remediation plan: revert the specific async_flush change in a hotfix release to dedicated and hosted clusters; schedule patch for 2026-03-13.
investigation_notes:
- Reproduction was achieved in staging with smaller thresholds; rollback of kernel selector removed the hang.
- Traces show stream_writer stops emitting chunks despite model backend continuing token generation (model logs show continued step progress).
- Memory and GC spikes observed when KV cache grows above 28M entries for rw-instruct-70b-v1.
- Candidate root cause: scheduling/race introduced in async_flush path (commit r3456) that can leave front-end stream writer awaiting a callback that never fires under certain batching sizes.
- Next step: engineering to prepare hotfix reverting the async_flush behavior and add additional telemetry to detect stuck stream writers in future.
resolution: Pending (hotfix planned). Temporary workaround: cap max_tokens to 25k and split large prompts. Engineering to push hotfix revert of async_flush changes in r3456 on 2026-03-13 and monitor customer traffic. If hotfix is successful, schedule a follow-up ticket to add a synthetic test for large-KV streaming to prevent regressions.
postmortem_actions: Hotfix: revert async_flush change from r3456 and roll to us-east-1 pools (owner: runtime eng)
Add e2e regression test for streaming with large KV cache sizes and high max_tokens (owner: QA/runtime)
Instrument stream_writer with 'stuck' metric and alert at >15s without emission for active streams (owner: infra)
